subject.title: Feature: configurable mediaLocalRoots for image tool

question: What public config and security boundary should OpenClaw support for operator-controlled host-local media reads?
rationale: The requested behavior changes which host filesystem paths model-facing tools may read, and the repository policy requires maintainer intent for new config/default surfaces and filesystem/media-root access changes.

options.title: Adopt shared filesystem roots
options.body: Use the reviewed `tools.fs.roots` direction, or a narrowed equivalent, so image/media tools, outbound media, and FS access share one policy surface.

options.title: Add media-only roots
options.body: Accept a smaller `tools.mediaLocalRoots` or `tools.image.mediaLocalRoots` surface, but own the long-term drift risk between media, channel inbound roots, and FS tools.

options.title: Keep managed roots only
options.body: Decline broad host-root configuration and keep users on workspace, managed media, channel inbound roots, symlinks, or copy workflows.

recommendation.title: Adopt shared filesystem roots
recommendation.body: Use the reviewed `tools.fs.roots` direction, or a narrowed equivalent, so image/media tools, outbound media, and FS access share one policy surface.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest recent path history across media access, image-tool, and filesystem safety primitives that the policy decision affects.
